top_categories.workout_context: Dirty Dino's Utah desert gravel rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Dirty Dino. Train it until it feels boring.
At Dirty Dino, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Dirty Dino's Utah desert, Local event forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 98 miles.
At mile 60 of 98, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
When someone attacks on Utah desert gravel, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Dirty Dino's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 98 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 98 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Varied gradients on Utah desert gravel demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Tempo is Dirty Dino's race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 98 miles on Utah desert gravel. Train it until it's automatic.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Dirty Dino, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Dirty Dino’s 98 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Dirty Dino requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on utah desert gravel to build confidence. Expect: utah desert, local event, mountain west gravel.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, G Spot, and Over Under to prepare you for 98 miles of utah desert gravel in Vernal, Utah.
